title: Israel votes: a referendum on Netanyahu?
lines: Israelis go to the polls on Tuesday, the twenty-seventh of October, in an election widely seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu.
All one hundred and twenty seats in the Knesset, Israel's parliament, are up for grabs.
A government needs at least sixty-one seats, and no single party has ever won that many alone.
According to polls cited by Al Jazeera, the opposition bloc is projected at about fifty-two seats.
Netanyahu's religious-nationalist alliance is projected at about fifty.
The main challengers include former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, and an alliance led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid.
Arab-led parties, projected at around thirteen seats combined, could decide who governs.
Netanyahu has warned that Iran or its proxies could attack to disrupt the vote, saying the army is ready both to defend and to strike.
The election comes eight months into the war with Iran, which began in February.
Possible outcomes range from another Netanyahu government, to an opposition coalition, or even another election.
Whoever wins will shape the region's path on Iran, Gaza and Lebanon.
